cost_rule: Casters only: Mana cost = the Power's Power Level - the character's tier Power Level (Novice 1 ... Legendary 5), minimum 1. Non-Casters pay the base Mana. Surge is paid in full. Basic Cast is free. (DECISIONS.md)
setting_the_power_level: The player describes what they want to do. The GM uses the scope guidelines to assign a level. This should be a two-line conversation, not a rules argument.
Flavor swap, minor range/duration shift, fewer targets than max: No change.
One tier up in a single dimension (more targets, larger area, or longer duration): Raise by +1.
Add a meaningful secondary effect (damage + slow, attack + reveal): Raise by +1.
Push two or more dimensions simultaneously: Raise by +2.
Player scales back scope mid-negotiation: GM may reduce by −1.
→ Weird Magic: The Weird Magic system — including the d20 Weird Table, Weird Fallout, Tainted track, and Dread interactions — is in the Overlays chapter.

weird.source: Book of Genres, Weird Magic. Tainted is tracked as Corruption (DECISIONS.md).
weird.when: Whenever you cast a Weird Magic Power, roll d20 after the Power's success or failure is resolved. The result applies on top of the normal Power effect. A Bane (natural 1) on the cast, or a Backlash or Revelation result, adds 1 Corruption.

table.name: Backlash
table.effect: The Power also targets the caster at half effect. Add 1 Corruption immediately.

table.name: Bleed
table.effect: The Power leaves a visible mark on the caster — a scorch, a sigil, a color in the eye. Narrative only; the GM tracks it and may use it later.

table.name: Echo
table.effect: The Power fires again next round at the same target. No Action or pool cost required.

table.name: Drain
table.effect: The pool cost drains from a random pool. Roll d20: 1–7 Mana, 8–14 Stamina, 15–20 Resolve.

table.name: Surge Free
table.effect: The Power gains 1 free Surge box this cast at no cost.

table.name: Stable
table.effect: No additional effect. The Weird was quiet this time.

table.name: Shift
table.effect: The Effect type changes to an adjacent type. GM and player agree on adjacency (Fire→Electric, Psychic→Void, Toxic→Cold, etc.).

table.name: Revelation
table.effect: The caster briefly perceives something they were not meant to see. The GM narrates a fragment of forbidden knowledge. Mark 1 Resolve box. Add 1 Corruption.

weird.fallout_when: On a Weird Magic cast, a natural 1 while Surging 3+ boxes is Weird Fallout instead of the normal Surge Fallout. Roll d20:

fallout.name: Uncontrolled outward
fallout.effect: The Power manifests in the environment (as Arcane Fallout). Add 1 Corruption.

fallout.name: Inward
fallout.effect: The caster gains Removed (Spirit) for the rest of the scene (as Spiritual Fallout). Add 1 Corruption.

fallout.name: Unravelling
fallout.effect: The Power fails completely — no effect, pool cost still paid. Add 1 Corruption.

fallout.name: Something notices
fallout.effect: The GM introduces a supernatural consequence in the next scene — an entity drawn by the signal, a shift in local reality, an uninvited presence. Add 2 Corruption.

notes: Weird Control (Willpower, DC 14): try to direct or suppress a Weird Table result before it resolves — choose between the rolled result and a re-roll. Succeeding twice on Weird Control in one scene adds 1 Corruption.
Weird Read (Acuity): after 3+ Weird rolls in a session, the GM gives insight into what the Weird is doing.
Witnesses to Weird Magic, allies included, make a Horror Check DC 12 when they see it cast. The caster is exempt.

The Weird Role changes these rolls: roll twice and choose (Step 1), Revelation marks no Resolve (Step 2), declare a result once per scene (Step 3), choose the Drain pool (Step 4), redirect Backlash to a visible target (Step 5).
